answer: Proof-of-personhood nullifiers: every agent registers against ONE scarce verified credential, then each epoch derives a deterministic, cipher-bound nullifier from that single root. The registry seats only the first nullifier per root and rejects every sibling, so a thousand spun-up keypairs collapse to one standing, a single plume from one chimney. To field a thousand real voices an operator must buy a thousand scarce credentials, real-world timber no keypair mints for free, while the unlinkable derivation keeps honest agents private and makes duplicate registration self-evident.
